cards.explanation: The answer is False. David says “…all people will come to You.” (Psalm 65:2) He doesn't limit it to Zion. He calls God the One who listens to prayer, and he says all people will come to Him.

The answer is that He atones for them. Iniquities prevail against David, and then he says “…You atone for our transgressions.” (Psalm 65:3) Notice he moves from 'me' to 'our.' He's honest about the problem and then he points straight at what God does.

The answer is blessed. David says, “Blessed is the one You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courts!” (Psalm 65:4) Chosen, brought near, and blessed, friends. I can't think of a better three-word résumé.

The answer is the goodness of His house. David says, “We are filled with the goodness of Your house, the holiness of Your temple.” (Psalm 65:4) Goodness AND holiness, friends. That's a full plate, and nobody's asking for a to-go box.

The answer is to the ends of the earth and the farthest seas. David calls God “…the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas.” (Psalm 65:5) That's about as far as a song can reach. The farthest seas, and God is still the hope there.

The answer is that He stilled them. David says, “You stilled the roaring of the seas, the pounding of their waves…” (Psalm 65:7) Stilled is the word he uses for what God did. The roaring and the pounding are the very things he says God stilled.

The answer is True. David says God stilled the seas and also “…the tumult of the nations.” (Psalm 65:7) So it's not only water, friends. The song puts the noise of the nations right next to the noise of the waves.
The answer is fear. David says, “Those who live far away fear Your wonders…” (Psalm 65:8) The wonders reach people who live far away, friends. Nobody has to be in Zion to notice them.

The answer is that He waters it and enriches it. David says, “You attend to the earth and water it; with abundance You enrich it.” (Psalm 65:9) God attends to the earth, waters it, and enriches it. Not a bad way to be looked after.

The answer is the people's grain. David says, “…You prepare our grain by providing for the earth.” (Psalm 65:9) He says our grain, friends, so it's the people's. The streams are full, and the grain gets prepared.
The answer is showers. David says, “You soften it with showers and bless its growth.” (Psalm 65:10) Showers are what soften the ground, friends. God also blesses its growth.

The answer is True. David says, “You crown the year with Your bounty, and Your paths overflow with plenty.” (Psalm 65:11) The year gets a crown, and the crown is God's bounty. His paths overflow with plenty too.

The answer is the pastures of the wilderness. David says, “The pastures of the wilderness overflow; the hills are robed with joy.” (Psalm 65:12) Even the wilderness pastures overflow, friends. That's not the first place you'd expect it.

The answer is flocks. David says, “The pastures are clothed with flocks, and the valleys are decked with grain.” (Psalm 65:13) The pastures are clothed with flocks, friends. The valleys are decked with grain.

The answer is that they shout in triumph and sing. David ends with, “They shout in triumph; indeed, they sing.” (Psalm 65:13) The pastures and valleys are the ones shouting and singing, friends. The song closes on that sound.
